display.purpose: Top-of-page titles, character name on detail, page greetings. One per surface.

headline.purpose: Section headers in long-form review, modal titles, named regions.

title.purpose: Card titles, dialog headers, active step labels in the stepper.

body.purpose: Running prose, chat messages, profile review text. Cap at 65–75ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, pills, status chips, form labels, sub-header pills.

mono.purpose: Inline code, pre blocks, tool argument previews, file paths.

shadows.name: glow-xs
shadows.purpose: Quietest. Input focus accompaniment, hover on quiet buttons.

shadows.name: glow-sm
shadows.purpose: Hover on primary CTA, active scenario card, streaming message.

shadows.name: glow-md
shadows.purpose: Focused dialog at rest, just-generated character on first appearance.

shadows.name: glow-lg
shadows.purpose: Hero CTA at rest. Uses Bright Violet because this is an alive state.

shadows.name: glow-ring
shadows.purpose: Active state on pills and stepper steps. Replaces focus ring entirely.

shadows.name: glow-rim
shadows.purpose: Hover on elevated cards. The room's light touching the surface edge.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default entrance curve and glow easing. Settles into place, never bounces.

motion.name: duration-tool-in
motion.purpose: Tool-call card entrance inside the agent stream.

motion.name: duration-glow-ease
motion.purpose: Default glow transition on hover and focus state changes.

motion.name: loop-thinking-dot
motion.purpose: Three-dot pulse signaling agent is working.

ambient.name: primary-wash
ambient.purpose: The room's overhead Studio Violet light source.

ambient.name: deep-undertow
ambient.purpose: Lower-left depth wash. Pulls the room into shadow.

ambient.name: cool-rim
ambient.purpose: Faintest cool reflection at the bottom-right horizon. Suggests a second light source without becoming a second brand color.

breakpoints.name: app-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum window width assumed for the Electron app.

narrative.overview: That moment late at night when the only light in the room is the screen, and the air itself takes a slight violet cast. Everything sits in that wash, and the things you touch hum back. The system is not restrained: it lets the brand color carry atmosphere, surfaces, accents, and signals as one continuous voice. Where the old direction kept violet rare and the room candle-lit, this one turns the room itself violet and lets the work glow inside it. Tonally: the page sits on a deeper, more chromatic dark (low-lightness violet-tinted neutral, hue 295). The body background carries three layered atmospheric washes that make the room read as inhabited light. Studio Violet itself is brighter and more saturated, with a partner token (Bright Violet) reserved for moments that should feel alive. Glow stops being a focus-only privilege and becomes the system's signature device: ambient on the page, rim-lit on cards, halo'd on primary controls, intensified on the thing you're acting on. The system explicitly rejects character.ai / anime / cyberpunk-game-HUD cliché: no neon hearts, no kawaii icon sets, no anime gradients, no gacha-rarity card grids, no sparkle confetti, no AI-magic gradient overlays sold as features. The neon here is architectural ambient light, not iconography.
keyCharacteristics: Dark violet-tinted neutrals on hue 295 with a high-chroma Studio Violet that carries the brand voice (color strategy: Committed, ~40-50% of any given surface)
Atmospheric ambient glow on every page: three layered radial gradients (primary wash, deep undertow, cool rim)
Tonal layering + violet-tinted rings for elevation, no drop shadows on chrome
Expanded glow vocabulary (xs, sm, md, lg, ring, rim) used as the signature device
Pure system sans, scale-and-weight hierarchy, type stays quiet so color and glow can be loud
Ease-out-expo motion for entrances and glow transitions, glow never strobes or pulses decoratively

rules.name: The Violet Hour Rule
rules.body: Studio Violet is the system's continuous voice, not a rare accent. It is allowed to carry 30-60% of any given screen across atmosphere, structure, accent, and signal. The dosage check is no longer whether you used too much but whether you used it without intent.

rules.name: The Bright-Violet-Is-Signal Rule
rules.body: Bright Violet (oklch(0.8 0.28 303)) is reserved for moments of intentful focus or alive-ness: the primary CTA focus halo, the active stepper pill, the just-arrived character card, the rim of a focused dialog. Never use Bright Violet for ambient atmosphere or for components at rest.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is shifted toward hue 295 with chroma 0.02-0.028. Pure grayscale is forbidden. Pure white and pure black are forbidden by the OKLCH doctrine.

rules.name: The Architectural Glow Rule
rules.body: The neon in this system is architectural: room light, surface rim light, focus halo. Never iconography. No glowing hearts, no kawaii faces, no sparkle particles, no animated pulses, no CRT scanlines.

rules.name: The Quiet-Type-Loud-Light Rule
rules.body: Color and glow carry the brand voice; typography stays unobtrusive. No display serif, no script, no separate UI font for buttons. Type is structure; light is personality.

rules.name: The 65ch Rule
rules.body: Any block of running prose longer than three lines is capped at 65-75ch. Streaming chat is exempt because the dock width self-constrains.

rules.name: The No-Drop-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Chrome surfaces do not use box-shadow for grey-tone depth. They use Desk Surface + 1px ring + (on state) glow.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-the-Voice Rule
rules.body: Glow has been promoted from focus-only signal to the system's signature device. Ambient on the page, rim-light on surfaces, halos on primary controls, intensified on the thing being acted on. Use generously but never decoratively.

rules.name: The Two-Layer Rule
rules.body: Page to Desk Surface to Lifted Surface is the maximum depth. Nesting cards three deep is always wrong.

rules.name: The No-Pulse Rule
rules.body: Glow does not strobe, pulse, breathe, or animate on its own. It eases on hover or focus (200-300ms ease-out-expo) and fades on state change. Static or transitional, never decorative.

dos: Do use Studio Violet generously: ambient page wash, primary CTAs, focus rings, link color, active state, rim-lit card edges. The Violet Hour Rule replaces the old One Violet Rule.
Do reserve Bright Violet for alive moments: focus halos on the primary CTA, active stepper pills, just-arrived character cards, focused dialog rims.
Do rim-light elevated surfaces: cards, dialogs, popovers carry violet-tinted rings on hover/focus.
Do layer surfaces tonally: Deep Night to Desk Surface to Lifted Surface.
Do use the glow vocabulary as signature: ambient on page, rim on cards, halo on CTAs, intensified on focused content. Match weight to role.
Do reach for a pill for state and a button for action. Pills carry glow-ring when active.
Do use ease-out-expo for entrances and glow transitions.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion for every animation and for glow easing.
donts: Don't ship anything that reads as a character.ai clone, an anime chat app, or a waifu card gallery. No glowing heart icons, no kawaii faces, no gacha-rarity framings, no sparkle particles, no glowing emoji, no anime-pink-and-cyan rainbow gradients.
Don't add a second saturated brand color beyond Studio Violet / Bright Violet and destructive red.
Don't use drop shadows on cards, dialogs, popovers, or dock panels. Elevation is tonal + ring + glow.
Don't use a colored side-stripe (border-left greater than 1px) on any callout or card. Single exception: the blockquote inside chat-markdown.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is banned everywhere.
Don't use pure white or pure black. The project is OKLCH-doctrine.
Don't animate glow on its own. No pulsing halos, no breathing CTAs, no strobing rings, no CRT scanlines. Glow eases on hover/focus (200-300ms) and fades on state change.
Don't introduce a serif display face, a script, or a third font family.
Don't add hero-metric tiles, activate-your-workspace empty states, marketing-page hero typography, or onboarding tour overlays.
Don't use an em dash in UI copy.
Don't nest a card inside a card inside a card.
Don't use the atmospheric gradients (primary wash, deep undertow, cool rim) anywhere except on the body. They are interior lighting, not a component pattern.
